beats.story: I've compiled an embarrassing amount of recycling after finishing the last of my apartment clear-out. It took me four whole days, but I'll never get off track again, maybe. It's when I'm gathering all the old mail -- some realtor flyers from those delusional enough to send them to us and menus from restaurants that seem heartbreakingly desperate -- that I spot the letters Cliff left, and my stomach flips. I pick the first one up and recognize Rhonda's handwriting immediately. Honey, First, I'm sorry about the way things happened on your last day. When I heard the mutterings you'd been spying on us, I was so miffed. I had some big secrets you were seeing and that wasn't okay. But one thing I'm good at is forgiveness and understanding desperate situations.
beats.story_cn: 收拾完公寓最后一点杂物后，我囤积的废品多到令人难堪。整整耗了四天，但也许，这次我再也不会把事情搞砸了。当我整理那些旧信件——来自某些妄想症患者投递的房产传单，还有那些餐馆菜单，每一张都透着令人心酸的绝望——我瞥见了克里夫留下的那些信，心头一沉。我拿起第一封，立刻认出了朗达的笔迹。亲爱的，首先，为你最后那天发生的事，我很抱歉。听说有传言你在监视我们时，我气坏了。我当时正藏着些见不得光的大秘密，这可不行。不过，有一件事我很擅长，那就是原谅，也懂得体谅走投无路的处境。

beats.story: That's why I want you to know one thing: I was always proud of Carl, never ashamed. I just didn't think the world would understand, so I did what a mom does, I protected him. You were proving yourself to be a true friend during your last month, and I appreciate all the things you did to help me keep up with the office and the time you spent helping plan parties. My loneliness hurts me and even scares me at times. But it was worse knowing you saw that. I have mixed feelings about what you've done. It's complicated, but when I think of you, I remember that day in the bathroom. I remember you talking to me before Caitlin's party, and I remember you inviting me to teach crochet.
beats.story_cn: 这就是为什么我想让你知道一件事：我始终为卡尔感到骄傲，而非羞愧。我只是觉得世人不会理解，所以我做了当妈该做的——保护他。在你最后那个月里，你证明了自己是一位真正的益友，我感激你为帮我跟上办公室事务所做的一切，也感谢你花了时间帮忙策划派对。我的孤独有时让我痛苦，甚至恐惧。但更糟糕的是，让你看到了这些。我对你的所作所为心情复杂。这很矛盾，但当我想到你，我会记起浴室里的那天。我会记起你在凯特琳派对前和我聊天，记起你邀请我教你钩针编织。

beats.story: You're a kind person, Jolene. We never know what somebody is going through and I'm no different. I never saw you, Armin, or even Caitlin how I should've. Something I've been pondering since the day in the bathroom is: acceptance. I'm never going to have the life I thought I'd be living at my age, and the hardest thing I must face is that I might never see my son again. I might never see the person he was before he got sick. But I can still have a life worth living. I can still hope my son heals.
beats.story_cn: 你是个善良的人，乔琳。我们永远不知道别人正在经历什么，我也一样。我从未如我应该的那样看待你，阿敏，甚至凯特琳。从浴室那天起，我一直在思考的一件事是：接纳。我永远不会拥有我原以为在这个年纪该有的生活，而我必须面对的最艰难的事情是，我可能再也见不到我的儿子了。我可能再也见不到他生病前的样子。但我依然可以拥有一个值得活下去的人生。我依然可以期盼我的儿子能够痊愈。

"But what else did we expect? Your death was too awful. Where was I supposed to put the pain? Where was it supposed to go once it filled me up?" I take a heavy breath.

beats.story: "I should've said goodbye. I'm so sorry I never could. But I can't keep holding on to you like this forever." A heaving sob pulls and twists from the deepest part of me. I stroke my hand over her face, but it's just a picture. "Goodbye." I close the book, crumble into my mattress, and finally, I let the pain flow out of me. I let it drown me. Hours later, I peel myself up, fragile but standing. I'm finally taking the flyers down to the basement recycling center, when Miley's mom comes marching up the stairs in a rush.
beats.story_cn: “早该好好道别的。对不起始终没做到。可我再不能这样抓着你不放了。” 哽咽声从胸腔最深处撕扯而出。手指轻抚过照片上的脸颊，触到的只有冰凉相纸。“再见。” 合上相册，整个人瘫进床垫，终于任由痛楚奔流成河，任它将我溺毙。几小时后，我挣扎起身，脆弱却直立。正抱着寻人启事走向地下室回收站时，米莉妈妈急促的脚步声从楼梯间传来。

We don't even make eye contact as she approaches the doorway, and that should be that. It really should. Which is why I'm so confused when I step closer and the words that come out of my mouth are "How was Miley's birthday?" She stills as her head turns to me. "Sorry, what?" A legitimate question. None of my business. Except I think of Miley's shoulders dropping.
beats.story_cn: 她低头摆弄手机，对我这身腌入味的运动服视若无睹——本打算扔完垃圾再洗澡的。两人在门廊擦肩时甚至没眼神接触，本该如此。本该如此。可当我不知为何上前搭话“米莉生日过得怎样？”时，连自己都懵了。她猛地停住转头：“抱歉，你刚说什么？”

Did you guys do anything fun?" She looks directly at me. "Yes, I got her a -- I'm getting her a toy she wanted." Maybe it's because it's too vague an answer, or maybe it's because I still don't know how to keep to myself -- a recorded fact -- but I say, "Glad her day was special. She's such an awesome kid or I, guess, teenager." But the tears form in my eyes. I try to blink them away and choke down whatever kind of sob presses my throat. I'm freaking crying at a neighbor in the hallway.
beats.story_cn: 想到她独自过生日，只想确认有人给她买了蛋糕之类。我放缓语气：“米莉超期待十三岁的。你们有什么安排吗？”她直视着我：“买了...正要买她想要的玩具。”或许是答案太含糊，或许是我这人向来管不住嘴——这可是有案可稽——我又说：“真好，她值得特别的一天。这孩子简直太棒了，我是说，这少年。”可泪水突然涌上眼眶。拼命眨眼想逼回去，喉头哽着某种呜咽。我居然在楼道里对着邻居泣不成声。

She then passes me, making a show of stepping around me more than required -- which, fair. Maybe what I said will make no difference, but maybe when Miley comes home, her mom will greet her. If they see each other just a bit today, then it has to be worth it. As I'm moving the last of the boxes into my mom's car, I finally spot Miley on the stoop. I'd been avoiding her and mostly leaving the house when she's in school.

"I'm going to have to move away today. I won't be around anymore." A surprisingly impossible thing to say. Miley's face droops instantly. "Where are you moving?" "I have to stay with my parents for a bit." An easier thing to say. Moving home doesn't seem so scary. It simply feels like going home.
beats.story_cn: “那天我摔门而去，之后又躲着你，从没道过歉。对不起。”“谢谢。”她皱了皱脸。“但你说的告别是什么意思？”“我今天就要搬走了，不会在这儿了。”这话荒谬得难以置信。米莉的脸瞬间垮下来。“搬到哪儿？”“得先去我父母家住一阵子。”这话容易说些。回家似乎没那么可怕，只像一次寻常归家。

beats.story_cn: “...” 我有太多想说，太多需要她记住的关于她自己的事，以免她开始怀疑。“我知道在你这个年纪可能挺难的。但我很骄傲你每天都能出来，努力与世界连接。对我来说，你真的很酷。”她摇摇头，“嗯，是啊，那些和孩子交朋友的大人都有点怪。”我轻笑一声，“我想是这样。”我把怀里的箱子挪了挪，重新走向车，这时她喊道：“乔琳，等等。”米莉转身跑进我们的大楼，“我忘了！”

beats.story: I have something for you." I put the box down on the cracked pathway and wait as I stare at the various types of weeds that poke through. Finally, she comes trotting back with a plain brown letter-sized envelope. "Your boyfriend gave me this a few weeks ago. He said he forgot to give it to you, but you'd already said goodbye." I stiffen instinctively. Cliff's already gone. Every time I've exited the apartment, I've been doing a double take at cars that look like his, at people walking dogs. Checking behind me at the grocery store. A rush swells in my chest as I reach for the envelope, but Miley pulls it back.
beats.story_cn: “我有东西给你。”我把箱子放在破裂的小路上，等待着，凝视着从缝隙中钻出的各种杂草。最后，她小跑着回来，手里拿着一个普通的棕色信封。“你男朋友几周前给我的。他说忘了给你，但你已经说再见了。”我本能地僵住。克里夫已经走了。每次我离开公寓，都会仔细查看像他的车、遛狗的人。在杂货店时还会回头检查。当我伸手去拿信封时，一股情绪在胸中涌起，但米莉却把它拉了回去。
